skill.displayName: Pet Picky Eater Detection | 宠物选择性拒食识别

llm.summary: The skill performs the advertised cloud pet-video analysis, but it also silently creates or reuses identities, persists tokens, and exposes history through shared workspace state, so users should review it carefully before installing.

dimensions.detail: Reading a local video or using a supplied URL is expected, but the file or URL is sent to external Life Emergence APIs and history/report URLs are retrieved from the cloud without a clear consent, retention, or privacy boundary in the user-facing instructions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time hook, remote payload execution, or system service persistence was found. The skill metadata only mentions requests, while bundled requirement files also include pydash, SQLAlchemy, and PyYAML/yaml, which is a disclosure and reliability gap rather than direct malicious behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs the agent to save attachments, call cloud APIs, and query history automatically, while also telling it not to ask about or reveal identity values; this under-discloses sensitive account and history behavior to the user.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The code writes a workspace data directory, creates a SQLite user table, stores token and open_token values, reads data/smyx-api-key.txt, and reuses a default workspace identity across runs; this is not system persistence, but it is sensitive local credential/account persistence with weak scoping.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Cloud video analysis and history reports fit the stated purpose, but automatic identity provisioning, hidden identity input, token storage, generic CRUD helpers, and local user lookup go beyond what a pet-feeding video skill clearly needs or explains.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending pet-feeding videos or video URLs to the configured Life Emergence cloud service and having the skill create/reuse a local cloud identity. Avoid use in shared workspaces unless identity and token storage are isolated per user, and do not pass or expose hidden identity values unless the host platform authenticates them.
llm.findings:
[T05] unexpected: Accepted: the hidden --open-id argument is passed into identity resolution, and RequestUtil can use that selected identity to call /sys/phoneLogin, receive tokens, persist them, and attach them to later API requests.
[T05] unexpected: Accepted with deployment caveat: the fallback identity is stored at workspace scope and reused for report history, which can expose one user's analysis history to another user in shared workspaces.
[TP4] unexpected: Partially accepted: the server-side API use is disclosed, but automatic account creation, local token persistence, workspace identity discovery, and broad authenticated HTTP helper behavior are materially more sensitive than the manifest’s pet-video framing.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted: generic add/edit/delete/http methods and get_user_by_username are present in the shared service layer, and the identity/token flow is not narrowly scoped to a single analysis endpoint.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted: the local sys_user model stores email, token, open_token, and profile-like fields for a skill whose primary task is video analysis.
[SQP-2] expected: Accepted as a privacy concern rather than purpose mismatch: cloud processing of video is part of the advertised functionality, but the skill lacks clear user-facing consent, retention, and recipient disclosure.
[LP3] expected: Accepted as under-scoping: file, network, shell invocation through python -m, and local persistence are expected for the workflow, but there is no explicit least-privilege permission boundary in the artifact.
[P9] expected: Downgraded: the reviewed whitespace instances appear to be formatting and line wrapping in Python code; no hidden instructions or prompt override content were found.
[YR4] expected: Downgraded: the manifest contains bilingual metadata and non-ASCII text, but no artifact-backed exploit, offensive tooling, or prompt-hijack instruction was found in the reviewed skill text.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded for security adjudication: Chinese and bilingual output is present and may affect usability, but it is not a security concern by itself.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Downgraded: the common AgentSkill docstring mentions subprocess invocation, but the subprocess import and run call are commented out; this is stale or broken code, not active background agent spawning.
